chunks: By Allah, they nurtured Islam as a calf is nurtured, with their hands being the whip and their tongues being the goads.
ai.seo_question: How did the early Muslims nurture Islam according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi presents this vivid metaphor to illustrate the dual method of the Ansar in establishing Islam: the 'whip' (sibat) symbolizes the firmness of action and discipline, while the 'goad' (silat) represents the sharpness of their eloquent speech and guidance. This narration highlights the active, hands-on role of the early companions in nurturing the faith, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the practical leadership and dedication of the Ansar during the formative period of Islam.
